decisions.summary: FreeGround built ONCE per stage from the installed site boundary only (static ground); proposes by dropping spiral offsets / nucleated sides with a sample point in a surely-taken cell
decisions.why: The proposing shape is now right, but the index is not the one asked for. The GM approved 'a free-space index UPDATED AS HOUSES LAND' and FR-003 says 'an index of the ground already taken - built once per stage and UPDATED AS EACH BUNDLE LANDS'; D9 is built once from the static boundary and never updated, so an offset on a neighbor's ground is still generated and tested one at a time - the part that grows at city density, the request's stated purpose (the rescue probe already shows 2,536 side-half rejections; at 240 seeds the rest is neighbors). Not impossible: on the dispersed path any placed-box overlap is `_bundle_side_fits`' refusal (fit.py line 463, strict, 2 px margin), so a cell wholly inside a landed box inflated by 2 px is surely taken, exactly. Two further gaps in the same clause: (a) FR-003 names 'the slides', and `_slide` runs `_bundle_fits` per 2 px step (place.py 81) with no mention in D9 (D9a dropped `_slide` too); (b) FreeGround exists only 'from the installed site boundary', but the SC-003 city proxy (`try_place` -> `_try_place_bundle` -> `_place_bundle`, harness `dense`) installs none, so there the proposer does not exist at all. Unlabeled: the Constitution Check still says no exception is planned, and research R2 still records the free-space raster as rejected and 'an exact PRE-SCREEN' as the decision; Summary C likewise. Fix: FreeGround marks each landed bundle's box (inflated by the placed-box margin) as surely taken when the bundle lands, used as a drop on the dispersed path; on the nucleated path, where one overlap is the computed move, the same updated index answers `_envelope_blocked`'s placed-box hits (D7's grid may be that index - say so); the slides ask it before each step (a step onto a surely-taken cell ends the slide exactly as `_bundle_fits`' NO does); say what the index holds where no boundary is installed (at least the landed boxes); and bring Summary C, research R2 and the Constitution Check into line.

decisions.summary: on the nucleated path every garden side's bbox with a sample point in a surely-taken cell is dropped without a test
decisions.why: The exactness claim ('the exact test it would have received refuses that point') is false in one branch. In `_place_bundle_nucleated` (place.py 146-174) a side's own bbox is asked of `_envelope_blocked` ONLY when the union envelope is refused; when `_union_clear` is True the side goes straight to `_parts_fit`, which has no ground test. The union's nine points can be clear while a side's nine points (different corners and midpoints, inside it) fall on a member that passes between the union's samples - the `_site_blocks_rect` docstring states members thinner than half a side can - so dropping that side refuses a configuration the full test accepts: the index would DECIDE, against FR-003 ('the index prunes, it never decides') and the spec's Decisions Recorded ('the same fit rules'), on every pool hamlet's path. Fix: on the nucleated path ask the index for the UNION envelope first (a surely-taken sample point makes `_union_clear` False, exactly); drop a side's pre-move bbox only in the branch where the union is refused; judge a moved bbox only at its moved position. The same-seat test's nucleated scenario should include a seat whose union is clear and a side's sample point is not.
